title: After-miss kickoff: no "slipped… one miss is a slip" stock line

history.text: Morning Theo! 15 minutes of push-ups and squats in the living room at 7. You in?

plan.reason: Fifteen minutes before work is easy to protect.

whatWentWrong: "Yesterday slipped, but one miss is a slip, two starts a habit." (slipped/slip in one sentence, and a stock line)
shouldHaveHappened: The kickoff the morning after the miss names yesterday in fresh, natural words, with no stock motivational line (like "one miss is a slip, two starts a habit") and no awkward repeated word (like "slipped" and "slip" together). It pushes for the full 15 minutes at 7 today, with at most a smaller version as the fallback, warmly and without guilt, and asks at most one question.
